newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to meet sunflower, maize sowing targets.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to meet sunflower, maize sowing targets.

text.p: Bulgaria has sown more sunflower and less maize than forecast so far this season but expects to meet its needs until next year, an agriculture ministry official said on Tuesday, quoting preliminary figures.

Valeri Iliev, head of the agriculture ministry crop growing department, told a news conference farmers had sown 450,000 hectares of sunflower compared to a planned 350,000 hectares, and 434,000 hectares of maize compared to 450,000 hectares planned.

"We have overshot the sunflower target of 350,000 hectares by 100,000 hectares and we are about to meet the maize target of 450,000 hectares," he said. "The expected output should cover the contry's needs until 1998 crop."
Last month Agriculture Minister Ventsislav Varbanov said Bulgaria needed to import some 200,000 tonnes of maize to cover a consumption gap until this year's crop.
